questions.question: What does 'Renaissance' mean in the context of European art history?
choices: A period of renewed interest in classical learning and new artistic approaches
A period defined by digital media
A single style used identically across Europe

questions.question: What is linear perspective used to create?
choices: An illusion of spatial depth on a flat surface

questions.question: In one-point perspective, parallel lines receding into depth appear to meet at
What is chiaroscuro?
choices: A pattern of repeated geometric tiles
The use of strong contrasts between light and dark to model form

questions.question: What is sfumato associated with?
choices: Soft, gradual transitions between tones and colors
A strict grid of perspective lines

questions.question: Leonardo da Vinci's notebooks show that he
choices: worked only as a court musician
combined artistic observation with interests in science and engineering

questions.question: Which artist created the ceiling frescoes of the Sistine Chapel?
What is a fresco?
choices: A print made from a woodblock
A painting made on wet plaster so pigment bonds with the wall as it dries

questions.question: Which subject is associated with Raphael's School of Athens?
choices: An imagined gathering of ancient philosophers

questions.question: What was one effect of wealthy patrons commissioning art during the Renaissance?
choices: Patronage helped artists produce works for religious, civic, and private settings
It made every artist financially independent

questions.question: Why did many Renaissance artists study anatomy and geometry?
choices: To represent bodies and space with greater observational and structural understanding

questions.question: Which technique helps create the illusion of atmospheric perspective?
choices: Distant objects use heavier outlines and brighter detail
Distant forms appear lighter, less distinct, and often cooler in color

questions.question: What is contrapposto in Renaissance sculpture?
choices: A balanced pose with weight shifted onto one leg
A figure carved from several colors of glass
A method of painting wet plaster

questions.question: How did oil paint influence some Northern Renaissance painting?
choices: It prevented artists from painting small details
It allowed layered detail, subtle effects, and rich surface textures
It replaced all panel painting immediately
It could be used only on stone walls

questions.question: What did the printing press help artists and scholars do?
choices: Distribute images and texts more widely than hand copying alone

questions.question: Which feature is often associated with Renaissance portraiture?
choices: A rule that faces remain blank
Attention to individual likeness, status, and character

questions.question: A Renaissance painting shows a tiled floor whose lines converge in the distance. What does this suggest?
choices: The artist is using linear perspective
The work is a relief sculpture
The image has no sense of depth

questions.question: Why is the term 'Renaissance' not a perfect label for every region and artist of the period?
choices: No art was made outside Italy
Artistic change occurred unevenly and differed across places and communities
Every artist followed one identical method
The period has no historical evidence

questions.question: What is one difference between a religious commission and a secular portrait commission?
choices: Their purposes and intended audiences may differ

questions.question: When analyzing a Renaissance artwork, what is the strongest approach?
choices: Identify the artist and stop there
Judge it only by its size
Connect its visual techniques with its subject, patron, and historical context
